content.text:
Great questions. Here's my grounded take, based on how your discussion feature actually works today.

## Should discussions be the place for interesting articles/videos?

Short answer: **yes, but be deliberate about it** — and the key decision is *not* whether to allow links (people will paste them regardless), it's whether you treat a "link post" as a **first-class post type** or just as free text that happens to contain a URL.

Right now (`lib/forum/actions.ts`, `lib/validation/forum.ts`), a topic is `title + category + markdown body`. People can already paste a link into markdown — it just renders as a bare hyperlink. So you already *have* link-sharing by accident. The question is whether to lean in and make it nice.

My recommendation: **lean in, but keep it lightweight.** The cleanest model is "share link posts live in discussions under a dedicated category" (e.g. a `Links`/`Reading` / `Watching` category) rather than building a whole separate feature. You already have categories, slugs, moderation, reporting, and image handling — reuse all of it. Don't fork a parallel system.

## Yes — add link previews (unfurls)

This is the right instinct and it's low-risk because it's **presentational**. The mechanism is the same regardless of type:

1. Detect the first URL in a post (or a dedicated "link" field if you make it a post type).
2. Server-side, fetch the page and read **Open Graph / Twitter Card** meta tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:type`, `og:site_name`).
3. For video/rich media, use **oEmbed** (YouTube, Vimeo, etc. expose an oEmbed endpoint) to get the thumbnail + title + author, and optionally an embeddable player.
4. Cache the result so you fetch each URL once, not on every render.

What you described maps exactly onto standard unfurl behavior:

| Content | Where the data comes from | What you render |
|---|---|---|
| **Article** | OG tags (`og:image` = hero) | Hero image, title, description, source domain + favicon |
| **YouTube/Vimeo video** | oEmbed | Thumbnail, title, channel, duration; optional inline player |
| **Tweet/X, Mastodon, Bluesky** | oEmbed / provider cards | Author, avatar, post text, embedded media |

## Other preview types worth considering

Beyond articles and videos, the ones that come up on a dev-focused site:

- **GitHub repos / PRs / issues / gists** — GitHub's API (or OG tags) gives repo name, description, language, ⭐ count. Very high value for your audience.
- **npm / PyPI / crates packages** — name, version, weekly downloads, description.
- **Code sandboxes** — CodeSandbox, StackBlitz, CodePen (oEmbed → live embed).
- **Dev video/audio** — conference talks, YouTube (covered), Spotify/podcast episodes (oEmbed).
- **Slide decks / docs** — Google Docs, Notion public pages, Figma (Figma has oEmbed with live embeds).
- **Images / direct media** — just render the image itself (you already handle images via Supabase Storage).

A good architecture is a small set of **provider-specific resolvers** (GitHub, YouTube, oEmbed-generic) with a **generic Open Graph fallback** for everything else. That way 80% of links "just work" via OG, and you add rich resolvers only where the payoff is high.

## The things that'll bite you (worth deciding up front)

1. **Security / SSRF.** Fetching arbitrary user-submitted URLs server-side is a classic SSRF vector. You must block requests to internal/private IP ranges, cap redirects, set timeouts, and sanitize the HTML you extract. This is the single most important thing to get right.
2. **Image proxying.** `og:image` URLs point at third-party hosts — you'll want to proxy/cache them (and respect `next/image` remote patterns) rather than hotlinking, both for privacy and reliability.
3. **Caching.** Unfurl at post-creation time (or first view) and store the result — ideally a small `link_previews` table keyed by URL — so you don't re-fetch on every page load or hammer providers.
4. **Embed vs. card.** Decide whether videos play *inline* (iframe embed) or just show a thumbnail that links out. Inline embeds are heavier and have privacy/consent implications; thumbnail-cards are safer and faster. Many sites default to card + click-to-load-player.
5. **Markdown collision.** Since bodies are markdown, decide the rule: unfurl *bare* URLs on their own line (GitHub/Reddit style), but leave inline `[text](url)` links as plain links. Otherwise every inline link becomes a giant card.

## My suggested scope for a first cut

Start small and prove the pipeline:

1. A `Links` category (or a "share a link" affordance on the new-topic form).
2. A single server-side unfurl function: **OG/Twitter-card scraper + YouTube oEmbed**, with SSRF guards and a cache table.
3. One `<LinkPreview>` card component in your comic design system (`border-ink`, `shadow-comic`) — thumbnail, title, description, source.
4. Add GitHub as the second resolver once the generic path works.

That covers ~90% of what people will actually paste (articles + YouTube + GitHub) without over-building.

All three recommendations confirmed. Here's the responsible path I'll take — security foundation first, UI last, each phase independently verifiable.

## Plan: auto-unfurl link previews in discussions

**Core principle:** the risky part (fetching attacker-supplied URLs server-side) gets built and hardened *before* anything renders. Nothing user-facing ships until the fetch layer is safe.

### Phase 1 — Secure foundation (no user-visible change)
1. **SSRF-safe fetcher** (`lib/net/safe-fetch.ts`) — the load-bearing piece. `https`/`http` only, resolves DNS and rejects private/reserved/link-local ranges (incl. cloud metadata `169.254.169.254`), validates the IP **at connect time on every redirect hop** (defeats DNS-rebinding/TOCTOU), caps redirects, enforces timeout + max response size + content-type allowlist, sends a benign UA.
2. **DB + storage** migration — a `link_previews` cache table (keyed by normalized URL) and a public-read `link-preview-images` bucket written only by the service client, mirroring your `forum-images` + ledger pattern.
3. **URL extraction** (`lib/forum/links.ts`) — pull only *bare URLs on their own line*; inline `[text](url)` stays a plain link.

### Phase 2 — Resolve pipeline
4. **Resolvers** (`lib/links/`) — generic Open Graph / Twitter-card parser as the fallback, plus YouTube oEmbed. Each re-hosts the preview image into our bucket, so we never hand arbitrary hosts to `next/image`.
5. **`unfurlPost(body)` orchestrator** — extract → dedupe against cache → resolve → store. Called via `after()` from `createTopic`/`createReply`/`createItemReply` so posting is never blocked or slowed.

### Phase 3 — Render
6. **`<LinkPreviewCard>`** in your comic design system (`border-ink`, `shadow-comic`) — article hero/title/desc/domain; video thumbnail + channel + play glyph that opens the source.
7. Wire cards into the discussion detail page and `item-discussion` from the cache (bare URL with no cache entry yet → plain link, upgrades silently once resolved).

### Phase 4 — Maintenance
8. Cron to refresh stale previews and reclaim orphaned preview images, reusing your sweep pattern; registered in `vercel.json`.

-- DevsAssemble — 0025 link previews (unfurled cards for discussion links)
-- When a member pastes a bare URL on its own line in a topic/reply, a cron-free
-- background job (next/after) fetches the page through the SSRF-safe fetcher and
-- caches the resolved Open Graph / oEmbed metadata here, keyed by normalized
-- URL. The discussion UI reads from this cache — a cache miss renders a plain
-- link until the row lands. The preview image is re-hosted into a dedicated
-- bucket (never hot-linked), so image_path is this row's own cleanup ledger.
-- Public read (all content is public); writes only via the service-key client.
-- Reuses set_updated_at() from 0001.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Cache table
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
create table public.link_previews (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  url         text unique not null,                  -- normalized source URL (the cache key)
  status      text not null default 'pending'
                check (status in ('pending', 'ok', 'error')),
  kind        text not null default 'link'
                check (kind in ('link', 'article', 'video')),
  provider    text,                                   -- 'opengraph' | 'youtube' | ...
  title       text,
  description text,
  site_name   text,
  author      text,                                   -- channel/byline (video author, etc.)
  image_url   text,                                   -- our re-hosted public image URL
  image_path  text,                                   -- object path in link-preview-images (cleanup ledger)
  error       text,                                   -- last failure reason when status = 'error'
  fetched_at  timestamptz,                            -- when metadata was last resolved
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on table public.link_previews is
  'Cache of unfurled link metadata keyed by normalized URL. Populated by a background job after a post is created; read by the discussion UI.';

create trigger link_previews_set_updated_at
  before update on public.link_previews
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

-- The sweep refreshes the oldest-resolved rows; this index serves that scan.
create index link_previews_fetched_at_idx
  on public.link_previews (fetched_at);

alter table public.link_previews enable row level security;

-- Public read: previews decorate public discussion content.
create policy "link_previews_public_read"
  on public.link_previews for select
  using (true);

-- No insert/update/delete policies: unfurling is server-only and runs through
-- the secret-key client, which bypasses RLS. This keeps members from writing
-- arbitrary preview rows (which would otherwise be a self-XSS / spoofing vector).

values ('link-preview-images', 'link-preview-images', true)
on conflict (id) do nothing;

create policy "link_preview_images_public_read"
  on storage.objects for select
  using (bucket_id = 'link-preview-images');

-- service-key client during unfurling, which bypasses RLS.

## What shipped

**New files**
- `lib/net/rate-limit.ts` — simple in-memory fixed-window limiter (`rateLimit(key, {limit, windowMs})`)
- `lib/links/actions.ts` — `previewLink` server action

**Changed**

- `components/forum/markdown-toolbar.tsx` — the `MarkdownField` Preview tab extracts bare URLs and renders `<LinkPreviews>` below the markdown

## How it behaves
When you switch to **Preview**, the composer calls `previewLink` for each bare URL:
1. **Cache hit** → returns instantly, no network, no rate-limit spend.
2. **Miss** → spends one rate-limit token, runs the *same* `safeFetch → resolve → re-host` pipeline, writes to `link_previews`, returns the card.

Because it writes to the cache, it also **warms it** — so when the post publishes, the card is already there with no "appears a second later" gap. A URL that fails to resolve just stays a plain link.

## The guardrail you asked for
`previewLink` is an authenticated "fetch this URL for me" primitive, so it's gated: **10 unfurls/minute per user** (cache hits don't count). It rides `safeFetch`, so internal targets are still blocked; the limiter stops someone looping it against a third party.

Honest caveat (documented in the file): the limiter is **in-memory, per-instance** — on Fluid Compute an attacker across N warm instances gets up to N× the limit. That's fine for abuse-dampening; if you ever want a hard global quota, swap the Map for Upstash Redis (the `rateLimit` signature won't change).

## My recommendation: don't categorize by media type

I'd push back on "Link / Video" as categories — I think it's the wrong axis, for a concrete reason tied to what we just built:

**The link-preview system already labels format.** Every unfurled card carries `kind` = `article | video | link` and renders a video thumbnail vs. an article hero accordingly. So a reader can already *see* "this is a video" at a glance. A "Videos" category would duplicate information the card already shows — and create dead-ends: where does a text post *with* a video link go? What about a post with both an article and a question?

Categorize by **why someone is posting** (intent), not **what format they pasted**. Intent is what people actually browse by, and every post has exactly one intent but can mix formats.

## Recommended set

| Category | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **General** | Intros, meta, community chat |
| **Show & tell** | *Your own* projects, demos, things you shipped (rename of "Show your build") |
| **Worth sharing** ⭐ *new* | Articles, videos, repos, threads you found **elsewhere** — the home for the link-sharing you originally asked about |
| **Tools & strategies** | Prompts, agents, workflows, how-tos |

The better UX for that isn't a category — it's an **automatic filter/badge derived from `link_previews.kind`**: a "📺 Video / 📄 Article" chip the system sets for free, letting people filter *within* a category. No authoring burden, no misfiling. I'd hold that as a fast-follow rather than part of the category change.

Here's where things stand and what I'd build.

**Current state:** zero analytics in the app — no Vercel Analytics, PostHog, nothing. Preview cards and markdown links go straight to the destination, untracked. So this is a clean, greenfield addition.

**What's already in place that I'd reuse:**
- A `view_insights` capability already exists — I'd gate the monitoring page on that rather than inventing a new one.

Because it only ever redirects to a URL we already fetched and stored, it is **not an open redirect** (the classic phishing risk of a naive `/r?url=anything` endpoint). Clicks land in a `link_clicks` table (link + which discussion it came from + signed-in user if any + timestamp), and the admin page shows top content by clickthrough, totals, and which threads drove them.

-- DevsAssemble — 0027 link click tracking
-- Monitor clickthroughs on link-preview cards (the shared articles/videos). The
-- /l/[id] redirect route records one row per outbound click, then 302s to the
-- vetted URL stored on the link_previews row (id-keyed, so it's NOT an open
-- redirect). Writes are service-key only; admins read via the DAL. A maintained
-- click_count on link_previews mirrors the topics.reply_count trigger pattern so
-- the "top content" view is a cheap ordered scan. Privacy: we store the link,
-- the source discussion, and the signed-in user id (null for anonymous) — no IP,
-- no raw user-agent.

alter table public.link_previews
  add column click_count integer not null default 0;

create table public.link_clicks (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  link_preview_id uuid not null references public.link_previews (id) on delete cascade,
  topic_id        uuid references public.topics (id) on delete set null,
  user_id         uuid references public.profiles (id) on delete set null,
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now()
);

comment on table public.link_clicks is
  'One row per outbound click on a link-preview card. Service-key writes only (recorded by the /l/[id] redirect route); admins read via the DAL. RLS on with no policy.';

create index link_clicks_preview_idx on public.link_clicks (link_preview_id);
create index link_clicks_created_idx on public.link_clicks (created_at desc);

alter table public.link_clicks enable row level security;
-- No policies: service-only (mirrors feedback/tweets). RLS blocks anon/authenticated.

-- Keep link_previews.click_count in sync. Clicks are never deleted, so insert
-- only. security definer + empty search_path matches bump_topic_on_post().
create or replace function public.bump_link_click_count()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  update public.link_previews
    set click_count = click_count + 1
    where id = new.link_preview_id;
  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger link_clicks_bump_count
  after insert on public.link_clicks
  for each row execute function public.bump_link_click_count();

## Play button — fixed
You were right, it was off. Two right-shifts were compounding: the triangle path sat right-of-center in its viewBox **and** I'd added `ml-1`, nudging it further right. ## Clickthrough tracking — shipped
Answering your original question: we are now.

**How it works:** preview cards link to `/l/<preview-id>?from=<topic-id>` → the route records the click (via `after()`, so no added latency) → `302`s to the real URL. It's **not an open redirect** — it only ever redirects to a URL already stored in `link_previews` (vetted through the SSRF-safe fetcher) and re-checks the scheme first.

**What's captured** (per your choice): the link, the source discussion, and the signed-in user (null for anonymous) — no IP, no raw user-agent. Composer previews use `track={false}` so your own authoring doesn't pollute the data.

**Where to monitor it:** **Admin → Link analytics** (gated by the existing `view_insights` capability), showing:
- All-time + last-7-days click totals
- **Top content** ranked by clicks (with 📄/📺/🔗 type)
- **Recent clicks** — what, by whom, from which discussion

**Files:** migration `…0027_link_clicks.sql` (table + `click_count` trigger mirroring `reply_count`, execute revoked like `bump_topic_on_post`), `app/l/[id]/route.ts`, `lib/links/analytics.ts`, `app/(app)/admin/analytics/page.tsx`, hub card, plus `id`/`sourceTopicId`/`track` threaded through the preview components.
